claims.claim_text: Barbara Lauwers's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Women's Army Corps.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA biography says Lauwers joined the Army in June 1943 and was assigned to OSS after officer-candidate schooling.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Distinctive exact indexed name, matching sergeant rank, Army context, and OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit sequence from Women's Army Corps service to OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: Bozena Hauserova is retained as a documented birth-name variant.

claims.claim_text: Lauwers's last documented civilian employer before Army service was the Czechoslovak embassy in Washington.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA institutional history places her embassy work after Pearl Harbor and before she joined the Women's Army Corps.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same CIA profile connects the distinctive indexed person to the embassy, Army, and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded as the documented civilian job immediately preceding Army service.
claims.match_notes: No job title is supplied, so none is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Conrad F. LaGueux entered OSS from the United States Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official CIA catalogue states that LaGueux joined the Army and then found his way into OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Distinctive full name and matching commissioned Army context support a high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit Army-to-OSS sequence; no civilian employer is identified.
claims.match_notes: The military assignment is not labeled a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Cora Du Bois was a cultural anthropologist who conducted field research before OSS recruitment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA profile describes her anthropological field research before OSS recruited her as a regional expert and manager.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare exact name and OSS context support a high-confidence identity match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The work is definitely pre-OSS, but neither an employer nor an immediate sequence is established.
claims.match_notes: Occupation is published without inventing an employing organization.

claims.claim_text: Franklin P. Holcomb's immediate pre-OSS assignment was an Office of Naval Intelligence billet.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Marine Corps history documents Holcomb's ONI work, Marine Reserve activation, late-1942 ONI billet, and 1943 OSS transfer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact full name and the article's citation to RG 226, Entry A1-224, Box 341.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly bounded ONI assignment immediately before formal OSS entry.
claims.match_notes: The indexed branch classification is corrected from Army to Marine Corps.

claims.claim_text: Holcomb studied at Georgetown University's School of Foreign Service before accepting ONI work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Marine Corps history places his Georgetown studies from 1938 until the 1941 ONI offer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed as the same Franklin P. Holcomb through the exact personnel-file box citation.
claims.match_notes: Student status remains distinct from employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: James C. Luce was detailed from the United States Navy to OSS Detachment 101 in 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA catalogue supplies the Navy-to-OSS chronology; Luce's signed wartime report confirms his full name, rank, branch, and OSS context.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact name and middle initial plus Lieutenant Commander and Navy Medical Corps identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit 1943 detail from Navy service to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The military assignment is not labeled a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: A probable match links indexed Jeanne H. Taylor to 1930s work on the WPA Index of American Design.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA documents Jeanne Taylor as an Index supervisor; the National Gallery records her 1939 Federal Art Project work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable only: name and OSS context align, but reviewed sources do not supply middle initial H.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely prewar work, but not established as the immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: This common-name case remains flagged for direct Box 767 personnel-file review.

claims.claim_text: Sherman Kent's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Coordinator of Information.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA catalogue says Kent joined COI in 1941 and remained as it became OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Distinctive exact indexed name plus matching Yale, COI, and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit institutional succession from COI to OSS.
claims.match_notes: COI is modeled as a government assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Yale University was Sherman Kent's last documented civilian employer before COI and OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA study identifies Kent as a Yale history professor and places his wartime recruitment after years of teaching and research.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Distinctive name and specific Yale-to-wartime-intelligence chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded between Yale employment and COI entry in 1941.
claims.match_notes: The employment claim is separate from Kent's later government assignment.

claims.claim_text: Stanley P. Lovell was probably working as an industrial chemist, inventor, and entrepreneur immediately before OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA catalogue gives that background when describing his October 1942 appointment as OSS Research and Development chief.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact distinctive full name with middle initial and OSS leadership role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate occupation; the source does not name an employer.
claims.match_notes: No organization is inferred from the occupation.

claims.claim_text: Walter C. Langer's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was his private psychoanalytic practice in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA catalogue documents his Cambridge practice before he became an unpaid OSS consultant in December 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed name with middle initial and matching civilian OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded private practice immediately preceding OSS consultancy.
claims.match_notes: Private practice is classified as self-employment.

claims.claim_text: Walter C. Langer's last documented civilian work before OSS was self-employed psychoanalytic practice.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The same CIA chronology places his private practice immediately before his unpaid OSS consultancy.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed name with matching profession, location, and OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the final documented civilian work before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Self-employment is not converted into an employer organization.

claims.claim_text: William L. Langer's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Harvard University.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard's institutional magazine documents his faculty service from 1927 and appointment as OSS Research and Analysis chief in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed full name and matching CAF-15 civilian leadership context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded Harvard employment through his 1942 OSS appointment.
claims.match_notes: The role is employment, not student status.

claims.claim_text: Harvard University was William L. Langer's last documented civilian employer before OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: His continuous Harvard faculty chronology leads directly into the 1942 OSS Research and Analysis appointment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed full name and matching senior civilian OSS role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last civilian employer before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Earlier Clark University teaching is preserved separately.

claims.claim_text: William L. Langer taught at Clark University before joining Harvard in 1927.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA catalogue documents Clark and Harvard teaching before Langer's wartime OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact distinctive full name and matching OSS Research and Analysis leadership.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented earlier employment, not the immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: Clark is excluded from immediate-employer counts.
